title: Deeper borrowed eyes: each member's place description also reads two further ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV3-Small blocks (96 channels, 4x4), alongside the 48-channel 8x8 level it reads today
hypothesis: Experiment 12 is the only design on this ruler that moved the held-out photograph out of the 6-14% usable band: swapping the from-scratch trunk for nine ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV3-Small blocks took truedop_2024 from 10.75% to 49.5% usable (false fix 7.0% -> 5.5%), with every other stage held fixed. That is a direct measurement that what transfers to a never-seen survey is the pretrained trunk's photometric/semantic invariance, and the remaining loss is now almost all abstention (45%), not false fixes (5.5%): when it answers it is right 90% of the time; it just does not recognise the place often enough. The training photographs sit at 96-98% usable at the same held-out viewpoints, so the gap is still the survey, not the viewpoint. Experiment 12 cut the pretrained network at its shallowest useful point (features[0..8], 48 channels at stride 16) -- the levels that encode edges and local texture, i.e. exactly the levels whose responses still change with exposure, season and shadow. In ImageNet-trained CNNs, invariance to colour, contrast and texture detail grows with depth; the next two blocks (features 9-10, 96 channels at stride 32, 128 m frame -> 4x4) respond to arrangements of parts (road junction + roof row + tree line) rather than their pixel texture. Giving the place descriptor access to that level, while keeping the current 8x8 level so nothing experiment 12 relied on is removed, should let more 2024 frames land on the same prototype direction as their training-survey twins, converting abstentions into usable fixes. This is distinct from experiment 5 (from-scratch extra stride-2 stages, which wrecked training fit because new layers had to learn whole-frame layout from three photographs): here the deeper blocks arrive pretrained on a million photographs and are only fine-tuned at 0.1x LR. Earlier-era exp 26/27/28 also used features[0..10], but under a region-holdout eval and six synthetic lighting buckets; their verdicts do not transfer. The weights are already baked: model/pretrained/mnv3s_features10.pt (verified at design time: loads strict into mobilenet_v3_small().features[:11], output 96x4x4 at 128 px, 576,464 params, and its blocks 0-8 are tensor-identical to mnv3s_features8.pt).
method: model/model.py only changes the trunk/lift of Member: the trunk becomes mobilenet_v3_small features[:11] loaded strict from model/pretrained/mnv3s_features10.pt, split into two Sequentials (blocks 0-8 -> 48x8x8, blocks 9-10 -> 96x4x4); two 1x1 lifts (48->56 and 96->56, each Conv+BN+ReLU) are GAP-pooled and concatenated into the same 112-d feature f that feeds the unchanged BatchNorm1d -> L2 -> cosine-prototype head and offset head. Everything else (committee of 2, cosine head + margin, belief pooling decode, confidence gate, training loop, augmentation, epochs, 0.1x trunk LR) is unchanged.
expected_outcome: truedop_2024 usable_fix_rate 49.5% -> ~57% (plausible range 52-63%), false_fix_rate roughly flat at 4-7%, abstention 45% -> ~38%; mission_score 0.560 -> ~0.48 (kept if < 0.560). Train-capture diagnostics stay ~0.02-0.05 (the deeper level adds invariance, not memorisation capacity worth mentioning). The standing check applies: an improvement must come through usable_fix_rate rising. Refutation: if 2024 usable stays <= 50% or false fixes rise past ~8%, depth of the pretrained descriptor is not the bottleneck and the next experiment should target the survey gap through training signal or decode instead. Size: ~2.4 MB fp32 per member trunk + heads -> total ONNX ~7-8 MB, inside 32 MiB; host latency well under 250 ms (exp 12: 2.65 ms).
init_strategy: pretrained:mobilenet_v3_small IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..10] (torchvision, BSD-3; model/pretrained/mnv3s_features10.pt, fine-tuned at 0.1x LR) + from-scratch two-level 1x1 lifts, cosine head, offset head
eli5: Last time we gave the model a pair of eyes that had already looked at a million ordinary photographs, and it suddenly started recognising Berlin in a photo it had never seen. But we only used the first, simplest part of those eyes — the part that notices edges and textures, which change a lot between summer and winter or bright and dull light. This experiment also plugs in the next, deeper part, which notices how things are arranged (this road meets that row of roofs next to that park), and that changes much less from one photograph to the next. The model keeps the detail it already had and gains the bigger picture.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: NEW: two independent copies of the first ELEVEN blocks of MobileNetV3-Small, pre-trained on ImageNet (open BSD-3 licence) and fine-tuned on Berlin at a tenth of the usual learning rate. Each now reads the frame at two depths: the familiar 48-channel 8×8 map (edges and textures, as before) and a deeper 96-channel 4×4 map (how roads, roofs and trees are arranged across the frame). Each depth is lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame; the two halves together are the same-sized 112-number description of the place

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each) - a compass, not a lookup table; the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: unchanged from experiment 12: pre-trained blocks (now all eleven) tuned at a tenth of the learning rate of everything else on the same cosine curve; angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, targets, epochs and views per epoch unchanged

implementation_brief:
ONE change: each Member's trunk is deepened from mobilenet_v3_small features[:9] to features[:11] and the place feature reads BOTH the 8x8 and the new 4x4 level. Files: model/model.py (main change), model/train.py (only constants/log strings/train_info that name the trunk). Nothing else changes.

model/model.py:
1. Constants: TRUNK_BLOCKS = 11 (features[:11] = stem + 10 IR blocks). Keep TRUNK_OUT_CH name but set it to 96 (deep level); add TRUNK_MID_BLOCKS = 9 and TRUNK_MID_CH = 48 (the existing 8x8 level). PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH = Path(__file__).parent / 'pretrained' / 'mnv3s_features10.pt' (already in the repo; verified it loads strict into mobilenet_v3_small(weights=None).features[:11] after stripping the 'features.' key prefix; 212 keys; output 96x4x4 at 128x128 input). EMBED_DIM stays 112; add LIFT_DIM = EMBED_DIM // 2 = 56. Do not download anything; do not touch mnv3s_features8.pt.
2. build_pretrained_trunk(): same as now but features[:TRUNK_BLOCKS] with the new path, strict=True. Return the full Sequential.
3. Member.__init__: t = build_pretrained_trunk(); self.trunk = nn.ModuleDict? NO -- keep self.trunk a single module whose .parameters() are exactly the 11 pretrained blocks so trunk_parameters()/head_parameters() keep working unchanged: e.g. self.trunk = t and in embed() run t[:TRUNK_MID_BLOCKS] then t[TRUNK_MID_BLOCKS:] (nn.Sequential slicing shares the same submodules; alternatively iterate `for i, blk in enumerate(self.trunk)` and capture the output after index 8). Replace self.lift with two lifts: self.lift_mid = Conv2d(48, 56, 1, bias=False)+BatchNorm2d(56)+ReLU; self.lift_deep = Conv2d(96, 56, 1, bias=False)+BatchNorm2d(56)+ReLU. Buffers in_mean/in_std, embed_bn (BatchNorm1d(EMBED_DIM)), prototypes [n_cells, EMBED_DIM], off_head Linear(EMBED_DIM, 2) all unchanged.
4. Member.embed(x): xn = (x - in_mean)/in_std; h_mid = blocks 0..8 (xn) -> [B,48,8,8]; h_deep = blocks 9..10 (h_mid) -> [B,96,4,4]; f = cat([lift_mid(h_mid).mean((2,3)), lift_deep(h_deep).mean((2,3))], dim=1) -> [B,112]; e = F.normalize(embed_bn(f), dim=1); return e, f. forward(), CellLocNet, block_mask, the committee decode, loss_fn, export_onnx, estimate_position: UNCHANGED.
5. Update the module docstring: add a short 'DEEPER PRETRAINED TRUNK (experiment 13)' paragraph describing features[0..10] from mnv3s_features10.pt and the two-level 56+56 lift; keep all existing paragraphs.

model/train.py:
- Import whatever constants it imports from model.model; if it imports TRUNK_OUT_CH/TRUNK_BLOCKS just keep them working (fix the import list if you add/rename constants; add TRUNK_MID_CH if you print it).
- The trunk log line (~line 404) should read e.g. 'trunk: mobilenet_v3_small features[0..10] ... lifts 48->56 @8x8 + 96->56 @4x4 -> {EMBED_DIM}'. train_info 'trunk' string (~line 486) likewise ('mobilenet_v3_small features[0..10], two-level 1x1 lift 48->56 (8x8) + 96->56 (4x4)'), 'init' string -> features[0..10] / mnv3s_features10.pt, capture_sampling string may mention 'features[0..10]'. The optimiser groups are built from m.trunk_parameters() and m.head_parameters(), which pick up the two new blocks (trunk group, 0.1x LR) and the two new lifts (head group) automatically -- verify the existing 'grouped' sanity check (every param in exactly one group) still passes. Trunk BatchNorm handling, augmentation, paired-survey sampling, epochs, LR schedule, diagnostics, chunking: UNCHANGED.

FIXED CONTRACTS (the frozen scorer depends on them):
- train.py CLI unchanged; training reads only buckets(meta, 'train'); nothing under model/ may open the eval capture (truedop_2024) in any form.
- train.py exports one ONNX per area at <out>/models/<area>.onnx via export_onnx: input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalised map coords in [0,1], conf in [0,1]; the whole decode stays inside the graph; opset 17, dynamo=False.
- Gates: fp32 ONNX <= 32 MiB (expect ~7-8 MB), host latency proxy <= 250 ms.
- Quick self-check before exiting: build the model on a dummy meta, run a [2,3,128,128] forward in train and eval mode, export ONNX to a temp path and run it in onnxruntime once; confirm output shape [1,3] and the file size.
